title: Data Lakes and Lakehouse Architecture
name: 8. Data Lakes & Lakehouse Architecture
description: Master data lakes and lakehouse architecture: cloud object storage (Amazon S3, ADLS, GCS), HDFS distributed storage, Raw/Processed/Curated data zones, Medallion Architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold), columnar formats (Parquet, Avro, ORC), open table formats (Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, Apache Hudi), ACID transactions, snapshot isolation, MVCC, time travel, schema evolution, partition evolution, metadata catalogs (AWS Glue, Unity Catalog), small file compaction, and data governance.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of a data lake?
options: To store only relational tables
To store diverse data in flexible formats (structured, semi-structured, and unstructured)
To replace all operational application databases
To store only machine learning models
quiz.explanation: A Data Lake is a centralized repository that stores vast amounts of raw data in its native format, including structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data, until it is needed for analytical or ML workloads.

quiz.question: Which of the following data formats is organized as a columnar storage format?
options: CSV
JSON
Apache Parquet
Apache Avro
quiz.explanation: Apache Parquet is a columnar storage format designed for analytical queries, enabling column pruning and vectorized reads. CSV and JSON are text formats, while Avro is a row-oriented binary serialization format.

quiz.question: In the Medallion Architecture, what is the primary role of the Bronze layer?
options: To store business dashboards and reports
To store highly aggregated analytical summaries
To store raw ingested data from source systems with minimal or no transformation
To store only machine learning predictions
quiz.explanation: The Bronze layer acts as the raw landing zone that retains the original source data exactly as sent, maintaining historical fidelity and enabling full reprocessing and auditing.

quiz.question: What does the Delta Lake transaction log (_delta_log) manage?
options: User login passwords and tokens
Committed table changes, metadata actions, schema versions, and snapshots
Only CSV file schemas
Network packet routing across clusters
quiz.explanation: The Delta transaction log is an ordered record of every commit made to a table, tracking added/removed Parquet files, schema modifications, and metadata changes to guarantee ACID properties.

quiz.question: Which Apache Hudi table type uses a combination of columnar base files and row-based log files to minimize write latency?
options: Copy-on-Write (CoW)
Merge-on-Read (MoR)
Read-only (RO)
Append-only (AO)
quiz.explanation: Merge-on-Read (MoR) writes updates directly to compact delta log files rather than immediately rewriting entire Parquet base files, deferring merging until read time or asynchronous background compaction.

quiz.question: What does Apache Iceberg's Partition Evolution capability allow data engineers to do?
options: Delete all historical table partitions permanently
Change table partition specifications over time without rewriting historical data files
Migrate from AWS S3 to Google Cloud Storage automatically
Convert Parquet files into uncompressed CSV files
quiz.explanation: Partition Evolution allows changing partition specs (e.g. from monthly to daily) seamlessly; existing files retain their original partition layout while new writes adhere to the new spec, and queries plan across both.

quiz.question: What is the primary purpose of file compaction in a data lake or lakehouse?
options: Increase duplicate records for redundancy
Combine numerous small files into fewer, larger, optimally sized files to reduce metadata and query overhead
Delete the external metadata catalog
Encrypt all database records
quiz.explanation: Compaction combines many small files (e.g. generated by streaming ingestion) into larger files (e.g. 128MB–512MB), drastically cutting object storage GET requests, query planning latency, and metadata overhead.

quiz.question: What information does a centralized metadata catalog (e.g. AWS Glue Data Catalog) provide?
options: Physical GPU RAM memory addresses
Dataset names, table definitions, column schemas, data types, partition details, and storage locations
Only raw unprocessed text records
SSL/TLS network security certificates
quiz.explanation: A metadata catalog acts as an enterprise inventory of tables and schemas, allowing diverse query engines (Spark, Trino, Athena) to discover and query tables without manual file path specification.

quiz.question: What does Time Travel enable in transactional table formats like Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg?
options: Real-time streaming ingestion from IoT sensors
Querying and auditing historical table snapshots and states using version numbers or timestamps
Altering the hardware server clock
Partitioning datasets strictly by time columns
quiz.explanation: Time travel allows data engineers to query tables 'AS OF' a specific historical timestamp or commit version, enabling reproducible machine learning experiments, audit verification, and instant rollback after bad pipeline runs.

quiz.question: What core paradigm does the Lakehouse architecture combine?
options: Only HDFS and MapReduce
Only SQL and Python script execution
Flexible, low-cost object storage of a data lake with the transactional reliability, ACID guarantees, and SQL performance of a data warehouse
Only CSV and JSON text files
quiz.explanation: A lakehouse combines the scale, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness of cloud object storage (data lakes) with the transactional consistency, schema governance, indexing, and high-performance SQL analytics of a data warehouse.
